name: Airtable
availability: Official hosted MCP, available on all Airtable plans. The Ompra package is an independent connector definition, not an Airtable endorsement.
recommendedAuth: OAuth through Ompra's existing MCP Reauthorize action. Airtable documents dynamic client registration for generic MCP clients; no borrowed client ID or bundled secret is needed.
features: Create bases and schema where the account permits
Inspect and edit supported automation drafts
prerequisites: Airtable account and access to the desired bases or interfaces
Browser consent for the resources selected during OAuth
Organization administrator approval where integration policies require it
limitations: Access is limited by the user's Airtable permissions and authorized resources
API quotas and base limits still apply; no additional Airtable MCP charge is currently documented
New-base creation requires workspace Creator or Owner access
Automation activation and Script actions require the Airtable UI
Existing interface editing and interface filters have documented restrictions
Installed does not mean authenticated or connected

advancedAuth.staticOAuth: Organizations that disallow DCR can register and allowlist their own Airtable OAuth integration. Configure its client ID in a local OMP MCP server entry; the portable Agent Plugin format must not contain oauth fields.
advancedAuth.pat: Airtable also accepts a personal access token in Authorization: Bearer. Add a separate local HTTP server with the Ompra MCP wizard and a user-supplied header, using only the required scopes/resources. Do not publish the token or edit the shared package.
advancedAuth.ompCaveat: Standard plugin headers are literal. Airtable's generic example using ${AIRTABLE_PAT} is not an OMP-compatible secret substitution mechanism. Prefer OAuth. A locally entered PAT header is stored in local MCP configuration, not guaranteed to be in an operating-system credential vault.

checks.status: Documentation, unauthenticated challenge, and advertised OAuth capability verified. End-user consent and authenticated tool execution remain untested.
